short: ISO 9001 is the ISO requirements standard for a quality management system; the current edition, ISO 9001:2026, was published on 16 September 2026, and organizations hold it as a certificate issued by a certification body.
title: ISO 9001, Quality Management Systems
subtitle: The ISO requirements standard for a quality management system, now in its 2026 edition
body_html:
What ISO 9001 is

ISO 9001 sets the requirements for a quality management system. It is written by ISO technical committee ISO/TC 176, subcommittee SC 2. The current edition is ISO 9001:2026, the sixth, published on 16 September 2026. It replaced ISO 9001:2015 and that edition's 2024 amendment on climate action, both of which ISO Open Data now records as withdrawn.

In ISO's own summary, the standard is for an organization that needs to show it can consistently deliver products and services that meet customer, legal and regulatory requirements, and that wants to raise customer satisfaction by running and improving such a system. Its requirements are generic, so it applies to any organization of any type or size.

What it covers

  • A quality management system: its scope, policy, objectives and processes.
  • Meeting customer requirements and applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
  • Customer satisfaction, and improvement of the system itself.
  • Assurance that what is delivered conforms to those requirements.

ISO notes that "product" and "service" in the standard mean what is intended for, or required by, a customer.

How conformity is shown

ISO publishes the standard and sells its text. ISO Open Data, the dataset ISO publishes for reuse, records the edition, the committee and the scope, and that is what this page is built from. It does not record who holds a certificate. A certificate against a requirements standard like this one is issued by a certification body after an audit, and it names that body, the edition, the scope and the dates.

What a claim does not mean

ISO 9001 is about how an organization manages quality, not a rating of how good its products are. It sets no performance level. It is not about security, energy or the environment; those have their own standards (ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 50001, ISO 14001).

ISO 9001 in data centers

For a data center operator, an ISO 9001 certificate says its processes for delivering services, such as colocation, installation and support, are run under an audited quality management system. It says nothing about the facility's power, cooling or security design.

  • Scope. A certificate covers named sites, services or activities. One site certified does not mean every site the operator runs is certified.
  • Edition. The certificate names the edition it was audited against. A certificate issued before September 2026 names ISO 9001:2015.
  • Certification body and certificate number. These let a reader confirm the certificate with the body that issued it.
  • Dates. A certificate has an issue date and an expiry date.

Related standards

Related management system standards on this site: ISO 14001, ISO 45001, ISO 50001 and ISO/IEC 27001. All are listed on the Standards and Frameworks hub.

Primary sources

  • ISO 9001:2026, ISO standard page (linked for readers; iso.org refuses automated readers, so the facts above come from ISO Open Data)
  • ISO Open Data, deliverables metadata: edition, publication date, committee and scope
